survey: Hiking backpack seen from a three-quarter front angle, standing upright on its flat base on the floor. Main green body with a top flap that folds over the bag. Two brown straps run from behind the top flap down its front to metal buckles. Each strap tip passes through its buckle and hangs below it, as on a real buckle. A front pocket with its own flap sits below and has a second pair of straps and buckles lined up under the first (four straps and four buckles, matching). Side pockets with rounded flaps are sewn to each side panel. A blue rolled sleeping mat lies across the top, held by two brown straps that wrap around it and go down behind the flap into the bag body, so it is tied on and does not float. The mat's right end faces the camera at an angle: E3 has a width ratio of 0.50 and is 0.7% off a true ellipse, which fits a round end seen at that angle. A brown shoulder strap runs down the back right edge from the top to near the base. The tools mark no loose ends or branches. The mat end is drawn as rings rather than a spiral, which is an acceptable simplification.
